data.body:
Root cause CONFIRMED with a purely local repro (no proxy, no network, no timeout).

init decided 'does the remote have a tickets branch?' by reading the LOCAL ref: init.py:367 ran 'git rev-parse --verify origin/tickets', which resolves refs/remotes/origin/tickets in the local object store - not a remote query. A full clone adopts the remote history; a 'git clone --single-branch --branch main' of the SAME repo silently bootstraps a 5-commit orphan, rebar list returns [], and merge-base exits 1. The same purely-local predicate backed the auto-init consent gate (init.py:645), which is why the reporter's FIRST command died with 'auto-init requires an interactive terminal'.

The agent proxy was a PRECONDITION, not the cause: --single-branch, --depth, a refspec-limited mirror, an interrupted fetch, or a branch published since the last fetch all reach the same state.

Authority: docs/architecture.md promises attachment when the branch exists 'locally OR ON origin', automatically, 'even with no TTY', explicitly for CI/agent/headless use. The doc said 'on origin'; the code implemented 'in refs/remotes/origin/'. This is the incomplete implementation of prior bug wet-chair-peg, whose regression test only ever covered the case where the tracking ref happens to be present.

FIX: one shared discriminator init.locate_tickets_branch returning local/tracking/remote/unreachable/none, used by BOTH the mount path and the consent gate. On 'remote' it fetches into the tracking ref with an explicit refspec then mounts; if the branch is known but the fetch fails it FAILS LOUDLY rather than fabricate a divergent store (AC2). 'unreachable' warns and keeps orphan-bootstrap so offline first-time init still works. Only the cheap ls-remote probe is bounded (15s) - the fetch itself is unbounded, which matters for the reporter's 49k-commit branch that needed minutes.

AC3: fsck now reports DIVERGED (no merge-base) as a real issue with a non-zero exit, and no longer mislabels an unrelated orphan history as 'ahead by N commits - push pending' followed by 'no issues found'.

ALSO CONFIRMED, NOT FIXED (out of this ticket's ACs): sync.py:170-173 gates its self-heal on the same missing tracking ref, and a bare 'git fetch <remote> <branch>' under a narrow clone refspec writes only FETCH_HEAD - so the --allow-unrelated-histories union merge at sync.py:96 is unreachable and an ALREADY-divergent store never heals itself. That explains why the reporter's store stayed empty all session. AC3's fsck DIVERGED report is the ticket's chosen remedy for existing divergent stores; making sync auto-heal them is a separate change and should get its own ticket.
